debian_pending.reason: Temporary acceptance of exact inherited Debian 13 findings in the development image while vendor patches and package removal are tracked. This does not assert non-exploitability. Do not expose this image as a production service.

kernel_headers.reason: Reviewed header-only attribution: linux-libc-dev owns userspace headers under /usr/include and /usr/lib/linux/uapi, not an executable kernel implementation. The 51 changed-version pairs are individually reviewed in .devcontainer/security-review-2026-10-05.md; CVE-2026-89972 is additionally reviewed in .devcontainer/security-review-2026-10-05-renewal.md. Evidence and remediation are in .devcontainer/security-remediation.md. Host applicability and privileged Docker-in-Docker remain open in cos-dam4 and cos-2jj7; cos-nxu6 remains their owner. This does not claim the host kernel is patched.

libxml2_pending.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-05 (cos-yi5p): all 8 advisories remain vulnerable in trixie 2.12.7+dfsg+really2.9.14-2.1+deb13u3 with no fixed trixie version; fixes exist only in forky/sid 2.15.4 (Debian bug 1146744). Debian marks CVE-2026-6653 <no-dsa> (minor) for trixie. libxml2 is inherited by development tools; do not parse untrusted XML in the image. Remove rows when a trixie update ships. Evidence: .devcontainer/security-review-2026-10-05-renewal.md.

openssh_pending.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-05 (cos-yi5p): Debian marks all 3 advisories <no-dsa> (minor) for trixie, fixed only in sid (OpenSSH 10.4). The image ships openssh-client only: CVE-2026-59999 and CVE-2026-60000 affect sshd; CVE-2026-60002 is a client use-after-free needing a server that changes its host key during re-key. Connect only to trusted servers with host-key verification. Evidence: .devcontainer/security-review-2026-10-05-renewal.md.

go_binaries.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-05 (cos-yi5p): 22 exact findings remain in prebuilt dolt v2.4.1 (Go 1.26.2 stdlib), bd v1.3.1 (grpc v1.83.0, thrift v0.23.0) and docker-buildx 0.37.1 (docker/docker v28.5.2, moby/go-archive v0.2.0). Each pin is its publisher's latest available release; syft and task findings are resolved. Update each binary when a patched release ships; tool input and registry access remain in scope. Evidence: .devcontainer/security-review-2026-10-05-renewal.md.
